executiveSummary: Surveillance reports from ECDC and PAHO spanning October 2025 through May 2026 indicate multiple concurrent public health threats across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) continues to circulate in the Americas region with ongoing animal and human spillover risk, representing a critical BSL-3 select agent concern. Mpox (BSL-3 select agent) remains active in the Americas as of April 2026, while dengue, chikungunya, and yellow fever maintain elevated transmission across Latin America. Additional concerns include pertussis resurgence, measles activity, hantavirus pulmonary syndrome, and the start of the Southern Hemisphere influenza season in late April 2026.
bottomLine: Multiple concurrent biological threats—including BSL-3 select agents H5N1 and Mpox—are actively circulating across the Americas and Europe, requiring coordinated surveillance and response.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple PAHO epidemiological updates in November 2025 and March 2026 indicating ongoing circulation
Zoonotic spillover risk to humans from animal reservoir
BSL-3 select agent with pandemic potential
Continued spread across North and South America in avian populations
threats.action: Enhance animal-human interface surveillance, activate One Health response protocols, ensure healthcare worker PPE and antiviral stockpiles, and report all suspected human cases immediately to WHO.

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued April 23 2026 indicating active transmission
BSL-3 select agent with sustained community spread
Ongoing circulation across multiple countries in the Americas
Risk of spread to European travelers detected via ECDC reporting
threats.action: Activate or maintain ring vaccination strategies, strengthen contact tracing, ensure laboratory diagnostic capacity for MPXV, and coordinate cross-border reporting with ECDC and WHO.

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update February 18 2026 indicating high case burden
Multiple serotypes potentially co-circulating increasing severe disease risk
Endemic expansion into previously low-transmission areas
Early 2026 data suggesting above-average seasonal activity
threats.action: Strengthen vector control programs, enhance clinical management capacity for severe dengue, increase entomological surveillance, and issue public health advisories for travel to affected areas.

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 13 2026
Epizootic activity in non-human primates signaling viral amplification
Risk to unvaccinated populations in endemic zones
Potential for urban transmission if Aedes aegypti exposure occurs
threats.action: Verify vaccination coverage in at-risk populations, strengthen epizootic surveillance in primate populations, ensure vaccine supply chains are intact, and issue travel health advisories.

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza and Respiratory Syncytial Virus
signals: PAHO alert January 9 2026 flagging simultaneous RSV and influenza co-circulation
Southern Hemisphere influenza season start signaled April 27 2026
ECDC weekly threat reports across April-May 2026 monitoring respiratory virus activity
Dual burden on healthcare systems from co-circulation
threats.action: Promote influenza vaccination uptake especially in Southern Hemisphere, strengthen respiratory surveillance networks, ensure antiviral availability, and prepare ICU surge capacity.

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two separate PAHO alerts in December 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained resurgence
Increasing cases across multiple countries suggesting waning vaccine immunity
Infants and unvaccinated individuals at highest risk
Potential for healthcare-associated transmission
threats.action: Review and reinforce Tdap vaccination schedules, prioritize maternal vaccination, strengthen laboratory confirmation capacity, and investigate potential vaccine-escape strains.

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 3 2026
Importation risk from endemic regions to areas with vaccination gaps
Resurgence linked to pandemic-era immunization disruptions
Multiple countries in the Americas reporting cases or outbreaks
threats.action: Conduct vaccination coverage assessments, implement catch-up immunization campaigns for missed doses, strengthen case-based surveillance, and activate rapid response for cluster investigation.

threats.name: Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert December 19 2025 indicating active transmission
High case fatality rate making even sporadic cases significant
Rodent reservoir activity linked to environmental and climate factors
Potential for person-to-person transmission with Andes virus variant
threats.action: Enhance rodent control and environmental risk communication, strengthen clinician awareness for early diagnosis, ensure access to supportive care in endemic rural areas, and monitor for person-to-person transmission clusters.

selectAgentSummary: Two BSL-3 select agents were identified in active surveillance reports. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) (BSL-3) is flagged as Critical due to multiple PAHO updates in November 2025 and March 2026 documenting continued circulation in the Americas with confirmed zoonotic risk. Monkeypox virus (MPXV, BSL-3) is flagged as Elevated based on a PAHO epidemiological update from April 23 2026 confirming active transmission across the Americas region. Both pathogens require enhanced biosafety containment for laboratory work and heightened clinical and public health vigilance.
amrSignals: Pertussis resurgence with two PAHO alerts within three months raises concern for potential vaccine-escape or antimicrobial-resistant Bordetella pertussis strains warranting genomic surveillance
No explicit AMR pathogen reports identified in current surveillance cycle; baseline AMR monitoring should be maintained across all bacterial disease investigations
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous co-circulation of multiple arboviruses (dengue, chikungunya, yellow fever) in the Americas suggests expanding Aedes aegypti vector range likely linked to climate-driven habitat shifts
Dual BSL-3 select agent activity (H5N1 and Mpox) occurring concurrently places significant strain on high-containment laboratory capacity and public health response resources

Respiratory virus co-circulation (influenza and RSV) documented in both January 2026 and the start of the Southern Hemisphere season in April 2026 suggests prolonged or year-round respiratory disease burden
Pertussis resurgence sustained across two consecutive reporting periods (December 2025 and March 2026) indicates systemic immunization gap requiring urgent catch-up campaign

GLP-1 receptor agonist medication misuse alert from February 2026 and methanol poisoning alert from October 2025 highlight growing non-infectious public health threats requiring integrated surveillance
ECDC issuing five consecutive weekly threat reports (Weeks 16-20, April-May 2026) suggests sustained elevated communicable disease activity across Europe
